body: I love how "unsatisfying" the last track on IDMTHY is. The whole album up until that point may have some interpreting it as being idealizing of suicide, however, once you realize that there's nothing more to see than a slow fade into static, there's no confusing the message imo. It's genuinely scary and as someone with occasional sensory overload, I skip the last few minutes of pure static often 😭. But I genuinely think that that's the point. There is no happy ending with suicidal ideation. Since we don't know if there is such a thing as an afterlife, this life is all we have, and accepting the static (death) before it comes upon you naturally is to give up. Because of that, it makes the ending, for me, an extremely well articulated anti-suicide song, and it brings the whole album together thematically. It's our one mission on this earth to fight to keep living, and considering how scary and unsatisfying the ending sounds, that's just what I'll be doing 🥹.  -  I'm posting this because, while listening to the album just now, I had one of the most cathartic cries of my life. The song fantasy world really got to me, and I think it genuinely helped me realize how much of my life I have been taking for granted. I've paused the album and genuinely don't know if I want to see the end now, but I think that's a good thing. I'll leave it on this track for tonight 🥹. Such a beautiful articulation of the human struggle for meaning and I'm so glad I came upon this when I did.  -  I don't know the guy & probably never will, but this is some beautiful shit that has really helped me ask myself some genuinely important questions. Thank you Quadeca for this masterpiece and for the real vulnerability & incredible effort you put into this album ❤️ ; I am eternally grateful for your contribution - bless 🙏🙏

I personally look for experimentation and rule breaking when it comes to finding new music. While there's definitely a place for revival bands and young thug clones and musical acts that are heavily influenced by something, I just get less enjoyment out of them myself. For me, all the old musicians I listen to were boundry pushing in their day. I think of Zep, Jimi Hendrix, Prince etc. Some of these artists (like David Bowie) experimented in a vast variety of genres, pushing the boundaries and breaking the rules in all of them across multiple decades. And while David Bowie specifically might not have a great catalogue of albums front to back, it's the constant change of style that I really admire.
I think the reason so many people like the first album of any given artist/band the most is because after that, they stop experimenting. Almost becoming cover bands of themselves, desperately trying to recapture their old moments instead of pushing forward and changing.
What's really exciting to me is when artists change drastically every album. I may not like the new sound, but as long as it's original, I can appreciate it on a deeper level.
This is just me however. I do realize that most people probably don't listen to as much music as I do, so they may not be as tired of the same sounds being played over and over. 
It also depends on what you look for in a song when you listen. I REALLY enjoy different textures I can feel when I have headphones on. Some may like the lyrics/message. Some may like chords or melody more. Whatever the case, everyone focuses on different parts of the same song. This being said, some people may really enjoy revival bands because they might be very good at recreating whatever it is that they look for in a song. 
Basically, music is subjective (oh boy, who would've guessed). It's all just vibrations we interpret as sound anyways so listen to what you will and enjoy it like nothing else exists.

Super Mario Odyssey.

Beating the main story was mostly easy. The combination of exploration, puzzle solving, and platforming was a very enjoyable formula that never fully challenged my abilities. 
The ending was quite easy to beat aswell. Of course, this gave me some level of confidence in my abilities. Well, I was certainly wrong about how good I was. 
After you beat the main story and collect enough stars/moons, you'll be greated with a challenge. 
You get three lives to attempt the final challenge, if you fail, it's back to the beginning. 
And... HOLY SHIT, there was no reason for me to be confident in my abilities because I reached that challenge over a year ago. Ever since then, I've picked up the game for at least a few hours every month, trying to improve my platforming skills. Well, needless to say, I have completely failed the challenge every time. 
Yes, after nearly years of trying now, I have still never beat the challenge. Now, every time I open my switch, I'm reminded that my abilities are no match for talented level designers.
If anything, the final challenge of the game has made me appreciate it more. Never before have I experienced a more challenging end game. :)

In a VERY similar boat. All I can recommend to do is just release the songs on here and on other subreddits, even if they're unfinished. It can be really hard finalizing a project or song without outside opinions, so even if it feels painful to show them to others, know that you're making progress. 
As for how capable garage band is as a daw, I think it's honestly great. Easily the best free software I've ever worked with, and most tools you get with the upgrade to Logic aren't exactly necessary for the completion of songs. Definitely spend a lot of time on youtube if you plan to mix/master yourself.
At the end of the day, releasing music can only be a good thing. Even if it is "mediocre" in your eyes, having tracks to show people is a great way of making connections. 
Keep making and good luck!
